Emmet County Assessor
Property ownership in Emmet County involves assessment rules, credits, exemptions, and review dates. The Emmet County Assessor’s Office values real property, applies assessment laws, and provides information about programs that may affect taxable property value. It covers homes, farms, commercial buildings, industrial property, and improvements.
Role of the Emmet County Assessor
The assessor’s office has a statutory duty to assess real property in its jurisdiction unless Iowa law provides another treatment. Residential, commercial, industrial, and agricultural property can all be included. Property is revalued every two years, with January 1 as the effective assessment date.
The assessor determines the full or partial value of new construction and improvements according to their state of completion on January 1. This work concerns property value, not the final tax amount. Counties, cities, school districts, and townships establish budgets and tax levies.
The assessor does not perform several functions sometimes confused with assessment:
It does not collect property taxes, calculate the final tax bill, determine the tax rate, or set Board of Review policy.
Its main concern is assessed property value, while taxing jurisdictions establish the rates used for tax bills.
Property owners have a legal responsibility to report changes or improvements to real estate. New buildings, demolished or damaged structures, remodeling, additions, heating or cooling systems, mobile homes, fireplaces, finished basements or attics, decks, patios and garages can affect the assessment.
Important assessment dates
January 1 is the effective date of the current assessment. Property owners may request an informal assessment review from April 2 through April 25. The local Board of Review accepts assessment protests from April 2 through April 30.
The Board of Review meets from May 1 until adjournment. In odd–numbered years, another protest period runs from October 9 through October 31 for properties affected by changes from Director of Revenue Equalization Orders.
Tax Credits and Exemptions
The office administers several Iowa property tax programs. Eligibility depends on property, ownership, use, military status, land management, or other conditions established by state law.
The homestead tax credit is available to an Iowa property owner who lives in the property. The owner must occupy the homestead for at least six months of the year and live there on July 1. The current credit equals the levy on the first $4,850 of actual value.
Military service tax exemptions are available to qualifying Iowa residents. Eligible groups include certain honorably discharged veterans, qualifying Reserve Forces or Iowa National Guard members, and veterans who served during specified periods. The application is due by July 1 of the first claim year. Required military documents must also be recorded with the county recorder.
The disabled veterans homestead tax credit can equal 100% of the actual tax levy for qualifying homeowners. After approval, the credit can continue while legal conditions remain satisfied.
The family farm tax credit applies to agricultural tracts of at least 10 acres farmed by the owner or a designated family member. A claim filed by November 1 and approved normally does not require repeated filing while ownership and the designated farming person remain unchanged.
Forest and fruit–tree reservations can receive tax exemption when statutory conditions are met. A forest reservation must generally contain at least two acres and 200 growing forest trees per acre. A fruit–tree reservation must meet specific acreage and tree requirements. Applications are due by February 1 of the exemption year.
Pollution control and recycling property may qualify for an exemption when certified as eligible by the Iowa Department of Natural Resources. The application must be filed by February 1.
Office Location and Contact Information
The Emmet County Assessor’s Office is located in the Emmet County Courthouse at 609 1st Avenue North, Suite #2, Estherville, Iowa 51334. The office phone is 712–362–2609, and the fax is 712–362–7454. Office hours are Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
